_comment: Answer-quality cases for ask_mailbox, summarize_thread, extract_from_emails and the experimental tools over the synthetic baseline mailbox (indexer/tests/baseline/corpus.py). A case id starts with its tool's short name (ask-, summarize-, extract-, brief-, check-); a summarize_thread case names a baseline thread ID directly (nothing is embedded) and its evidence must be in that thread, and an extract_from_emails case gives its query and schema with a small limit, since each searched thread is one paid model call (the per-tool argument rules are in cases.py). Synthetic data only: never add a case built from a real mailbox. Message refs 'tNN.M' mean 'tNN.M@baseline.example'; thread refs 'tNN' mean the thread rooted at 'tNN.1@baseline.example'. required_evidence is a list of groups: every group is required and any one ref inside a group satisfies it. Each expected fact lists the message refs and a short verbatim excerpt of the indexed text that establishes it; make baseline checks each excerpt is in that message's indexed text, so references stay independent of what the system retrieves. deterministic.must_include is a list of groups of acceptable spellings (every group required, any spelling in a group satisfies it, case-insensitive substring of the answer). must_include checks that a value is present, not that the answer asserts it: an answer that names the value only to deny or correct it still passes, so correctness needs the judge. must_not_include lists strings no answer may contain. criteria say which rubric dimensions apply; the judge may not mark an applicable one not_applicable. held_out must equal tests/agent_metrics.py is_held_out(id); never tune against held-out cases. review records that the expected facts were drafted with AI from the synthetic corpus and await owner verification. An optional chronology object (#291) holds golden labels: positions (id, accepted actor names, kind, the one message ref stating it, its date and date_source sent or mentioned, the whole values that message states for it, and a verbatim excerpt), changes (from, to, kind) whose two sources an answer must both cite, conflicts whose every side it must cite, in_force (the positions as of as_of, or now when as_of is null) and as_of; every source an answer must cite is also a required_evidence group of its own.
